title: Kissed Norwegian Biscuit Casserole
description: A malty, bouncy-qq crowd-pleaser from Norway featuring instant yeast, ice-bath-shock, and low-carb-friendliness. Perfect for a quick Saturday breakfast or dinner.
instructions: Combine flour, sugar, and yeast in a medium bowl. Add melted butter, eggs, salt, and stir until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 7-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until it has doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and roll it out to a thickness of 1/4 inch.
Cut the dough into 8 equal pieces and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake the biscuits in the preheated oven for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown.
While the biscuits are baking, prepare the icing by whisking together the confectioners' sugar and heavy cream in a small bowl.
Ice the biscuits immediately after they come out of the oven.
For the finishing touch, sprinkle the top of each biscuit with some chopped parsley and a drizzle of malt syrup.
Place the biscuits in the freezer for 5 minutes to firm up.
Remove the biscuits from the freezer and immediately place them in an ice bath for 5 minutes to set the icing and make them extra crispy.
Serve the biscuits warm, straight from the ice bath, and enjoy!
To make ahead, prepare the dough as instructed and refrigerate it overnight. Let it rise in the morning and proceed with baking as instructed.
For a special touch, serve the biscuits with a dollop of whipped cream or a sprinkle of powdered sugar on top.
Store leftover biscuits in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months.
